 The Nevada men’s basketball team plays UC Santa Barbara on Wednesday at The Thunderdome. Nevada Sports Net's Chris Murray breaks down the game with his three keys to victory and prediction. This feature is presented in partnership with Bradley, Drendel & Jeanney .
 Nevada (2-0) at UC Santa Barbara (2-0) 
 When: Wednesday, 6 p.m.
 Where: The Thunderdome (5,000 capacity)
 TV/Radio: None/95.5 FM
 Online: ESPN+
 Betting line: No line listed yet
 Three keys for Nevada to win 
 1. Epic ball pressure: Nevada’s defense went from excellent against Robert Morris (73.2 points per 100 possessions) to not-so-good against Saint Mary’s (114.1 points per 100 possessions). Part of that was Robert Morris’ offense is bad and Saint Mary’s offense is good. But Nevada will face another good offense in UCSB, which is averaging 87.5 points per game. The Gauchos are shooting 50.9 percent from the field and 52.1 percent from three while also averaging 21 free throws per game and grabbing 12 offensive boards a game. That was in games against Division II San Francisco State and Oakland, a lower-level Division I team. But this is a strong offensive team with good balance and a variety of ways to score. Nevada’s on-ball pressure must be elite to limit the Gauchos’ offensive attack.
 2. Suffocate Aidan Mahaney: UCSB has four players averaging double-figures in scoring with eight guys averaging at least eight points per game. But the star of the show is Mahaney, who was a two-time All-WCC first-team honoree at Saint Mary's before a season at UConn and last year at UCSB. Nevada faced Mahaney a season ago and limited him to 10 points on 4-of-16 shooting, including 2-of-8 from three. The Wolf Pack suffocated Mahaney in that game and will look to do the same Wednesday. While an excellent player, Mahaney has been prone to duds. Last season, he had games where he shot 5-of-16, 5-of-18, 4-of-16, 3-of-15, 1-of-12 and 1-of-13. Mahaney can go ice cold, but he also posted eight games last season with 20-plus points, including a 30-point outburst. He’s erratic but dangerous.
 3. Clean offensive effort: Under Steve Alford, the Wolf Pack has done an excellent job of valuing the ball. Nevada had just 10 turnovers per game last season and hasn’t exceed 10.3 turnovers per game in any of the last four years. The Wolf Pack has hit that standard again this year, averaging just 10 turnovers in its first to games. UCSB, meanwhile, is forcing 15 turnovers per game, with seven steals and 5.5 blocks per contest. The Gauchos’ defense isn’t the stiffest, but the team does have good length and can get into passing lanes. If Nevada avoids turnovers in this game – it historically has – it should have success against UCSB’s defense. The Wolf Pack is averaging 91 points per game, so this is a favorable matchup as long as Nevada takes care of the ball.
 Prediction 
 Nevada 78, UC Santa Barbara 73: Both teams enter this game 2-0 with the Wolf Pack having the best win (by far) after beating Saint Mary’s in overtime Sunday. It’s a quick road trip to Southern California after a draining game, so Nevada’s energy will be tested against a team that has averaged 21 wins a game under 10th-year head coach Joe Pasternack. This looks to be a high-level offensive team with Weber State transfer Viljami Vartiainen, FIU transfer Eric Dibami and New Mexico transfer Antonio Chol all averaging double-figures alongside Mahaney, who is the key piece for UCSB. If Nevada slows him down, it will win. Season record: 2-0
